stories.title: US Imposes Sweeping Sanctions on International Criminal Court
stories.summary: The Trump administration has announced sweeping new sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC), aiming to dismantle the tribunal, which it claims is politicized and has attempted to prosecute Americans and Israelis illegally. The ICC has condemned the sanctions as an assault on the rule of law. In response, the European Union expressed readiness to support the court's operations.

stories.title: US Sanctions ICC Following Nobel Prize Award to Former Judge
stories.summary: The United States imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) shortly after former judge Navi Pillay was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her contributions to peace and international law. The ICC's deputy prosecutor condemned the sanctions, asserting that they would not impede the tribunal's operations.

stories.title: Navi Pillay Receives 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for Contributions to International Justice
stories.summary: Navi Pillay, a South African jurist and former UN human rights chief, has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law. The Norwegian Nobel Committee recognized her work, including her role as chair of a UN commission that concluded Israel committed genocide in Gaza. Pillay currently serves as a judge at the International Court of Justice.

stories.title: Three Saudis Killed in Houthi Strikes on Riyadh Airport
stories.summary: Three Saudi citizens, including an airline pilot, were killed in missile strikes on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which were claimed by Yemen's Houthi rebels. The attack occurred on October 8 and is reported to be the deadliest in Saudi Arabia since the kingdom launched a major military offensive against the Houthis the previous weekend. Several others were also wounded in the incident.

stories.title: Russian Strikes on Public Buses in Ukraine Result in Significant Casualties Amid Ongoing Attacks
stories.summary: A recent Russian strike on public buses in eastern Ukraine has resulted in at least 30 fatalities and numerous injuries. The attack occurred near a bus stop in Kramatorsk, coinciding with worsening power outages in Kyiv as the region faces an increase in military assaults. Authorities report that the situation remains dire, with ongoing attacks contributing to a humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Legendary NFL Coach Mike Ditka Passes Away at 86
stories.summary: Mike Ditka, the Hall of Fame coach known for leading the Chicago Bears to their only Super Bowl victory in 1985, has died at the age of 86. He was celebrated for his toughness and leadership, becoming an iconic figure in NFL history. His family described him as the heart of their family in their announcement of his passing.

stories.title: Violent Protests Erupt in South Africa Over Asylum Ruling
stories.summary: Protests in Soweto and Durban turned violent following a Constitutional Court ruling that eased restrictions on asylum applications. Demonstrators opposed the decision, leading to vehicles being torched and shops looted. In response to the unrest, the South African government has withdrawn the controversial asylum directive.

stories.title: ICE Officer Shoots Man During Arrest in New York
stories.summary: An ICE officer shot a Dominican man in the neck while attempting to make an arrest in New York. The incident occurred as the man was driving with a 5-year-old boy. Eyewitnesses reported hearing multiple gunshots as masked officers surrounded the vehicle. The Department of Homeland Security stated that the operation was part of a targeted enforcement effort.

stories.title: Massive Protests in Madrid Honor Evicted Pensioner Maricarmen Abascal
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of people marched in Madrid to honor Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old pensioner whose eviction became a symbol of Spain's housing crisis. Her recent death has intensified protests, with mourners gathering at Puerta del Sol, the movement's focal point. The protests reflect widespread anger and grief over housing issues in Spain.

stories.title: South Korea to Recall Ambassador to Ukraine Amid North Korean POW Dispute
stories.summary: South Korea has announced it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine due to a dispute over the public disclosure of North Korean prisoners of war at the UN. The decision follows South Korea's demand for an apology from Ukraine, which has not been received. In response, Ukraine expressed its willingness to engage in 'constructive dialogue' despite the diplomatic tensions.

stories.title: Recovered Renoir Paintings Linked to Museum Theft; Six Arrested
stories.summary: Two paintings by Pierre-Auguste Renoir, stolen from a museum in southern France, have been recovered. The artworks were seized after thieves broke into the Renoir Museum by cutting through a fence and smashing a window. Six individuals have been arrested in connection with the theft.

stories.title: US to Livestream Execution of Fort Hood Shooter Nidal Hasan
stories.summary: The Pentagon has announced that the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, who killed 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, will be livestreamed. The execution is scheduled for December 3 and will be conducted by firing squad, marking the first such military execution in the US since World War II.
